drug_class: Targeted therapy / EGFR inhibitor (a type of cancer medicine called a kinase inhibitor)
purpose: Osimertinib is used to treat a certain type of lung cancer called non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). It is used when the cancer has a specific change (mutation) in a gene called EGFR. Your doctor may use it after surgery to help prevent the cancer from coming back, or to treat cancer that has spread to other parts of the body.
how_it_works: Your lung cancer has a specific genetic change (EGFR mutation) that tells cancer cells to grow out of control. Osimertinib works like a targeted missile — it zeroes in on the abnormal EGFR protein that is driving the cancer and blocks it from working. This slows down or stops the cancer cells from growing and spreading, while causing less harm to normal healthy cells compared to traditional chemotherapy.
common_side_effects: Skin rash or acne-like breakouts (very common), dry or itchy skin, mouth sores, diarrhea, dry eyes or vision changes, nail problems (like soreness around the nails), tiredness, and loss of appetite. Some people may also notice swelling in the hands or feet.
warnings: Osimertinib can rarely cause serious lung problems (called interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis) — tell your doctor right away if you develop new or worsening shortness of breath or cough. It can affect your heart rhythm (QT prolongation) and heart function, so your doctor will monitor your heart with ECGs. It may also cause liver problems, so blood tests will be done regularly. This medicine can harm an unborn baby, so do not become pregnant or father a child while taking it — use reliable birth control during treatment and for some time after. Always tell your doctor about all other medicines you take, as some medications can interfere with how osimertinib works.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one 80 mg tablet taken by mouth once a day. Your doctor may lower the dose to 40 mg once daily if you have side effects. You can take it with or without food, at the same time each day. Swallow the tablet whole, but if you have trouble swallowing, you can dissolve it in water as instructed.
